# Iwahori Fundamental Local Equivalence

**Authors:** Taeuk Nam

## Abstract

We construct three tamely ramified local equivalences of factorization module categories. The first is a factorization version of the Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov equivalence at a point. The second is a factorization version of the Bezrukavnikov equivalence at a point. The third is an Iwahori-ramified version of the factorizable Fundamental Local Equivalence.

## Introduction

### 0.1. Motivation

#### 0.1.1.

The (de Rham, global, critical level) unramified geometric Langlands conjecture was recently proven in a series of five papers [GR24a], [ABC+24a], [CCF+24], [ABC+24b], and [GR24b] by nine authors: Arinkin, Beraldo, Campbell, Chen, Faergeman, Gaitsgory, Lin, Raskin, and Rozenblyum. The statement is that there is an equivalence of DG categories

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G})\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}}) $$

satisfying some compatibilities.

#### 0.1.2.

In the first paper, [GR24a], the authors construct the Langlands functor

$$ \mathbb{L}_{G}:\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G})\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}}). $$

The main ingredients of the construction are the spectral action

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}})\otimes\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G})\to\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G}) $$

and the fact that

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G}) $$

is a compactly generated DG category.

#### 0.1.3.

In the second paper, [ABC+24a], the Langlands functor is studied locally. More precisely, we mean the following.

#### 0.1.4.

At a point $x\in X$ , we can consider three equivalences of a local nature. These are the geometric Casselman-Shalika equivalence

$$ \operatorname{CS}_{G,x}:\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)_{x}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})_{x}, $$

the geometric Satake equivalence

$$ \operatorname{Sat}_{G,x}:\operatorname{Sph}_{G,x}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{spec}}, $$

and the Fundamental Local Equivalence (at critical level)

$$ \operatorname{FLE}_{G,x}:\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}). $$

Furthermore, the geometric Satake equivalence is an equivalence of monoidal categories. There is an action of $\operatorname{Sph}_{G,x}$ on $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)_{x}$ (resp. $\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x}$ ) and an action of $\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ on $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})_{x}$ (resp. $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{mon-free}})$ ). $\operatorname{CS}_{G,x}$ (resp. $\operatorname{FLE}_{G,x}$ ) is compatible with these actions under $\operatorname{Sat}_{G,x}$ .

#### 0.1.5.

These equivalences are shown to be compatible with the Langlands functor in loc. cit. in the following sense: there are commutative diagrams

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)_{x}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})_{x}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}).}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{CS}_{G,x}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{L}_{G}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{FLE}_{G,x}} $$

Furthermore, there is an action of $\operatorname{Sph}_{G,x}$ on $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G})$ and an action of $\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ on $\operatorname{IndCoh}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}})$ . $\mathbb{L}_{G}$ is compatible with these actions under $\operatorname{Sat}_{G,x}$ .

#### 0.1.6.

However, this is insufficient to control the behaviour of the global Langlands functor. Instead of choosing a point $x\in X$ , we must consider all points of $X$ simultaneously. Not only that, we also want to allow these points to ”move around in $X$ ”, or in other words, we want to allow $x$ to vary in families. In addition, we want to consider what happens when the points ”collide with each other” while moving around in $X$ , or in other words, we want to also allow families of tuples of points of $X$ .

#### 0.1.7.

It turns out that the correct technical device to employ in order to encode the above information is Factorization. The above equivalences are restrictions to a point $x\in\operatorname{Ran}$ of equivalences of factorization categories

$$ \operatorname{CS}_{G}:\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}), $$

$$ \operatorname{Sat}_{G}:\operatorname{Sph}_{G}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}, $$

and

$$ \operatorname{FLE}_{G}:\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}). $$

#### 0.1.8.

If we consider tame (Iwahori) ramification at a fixed point $x_{0}\in X$ in the context of global geometric Langlands, we are naturally led to ask: can we find a spectral description of the DG category of D-modules on $\operatorname{Bun}_{G}$ with Iwahori level structure? In other words, what should be on the right hand side of

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G}^{\operatorname{I}})\simeq\ ? $$

#### 0.1.9.

We have strong heuristic reasons to expect that the answer should be Ind-coherent sheaves (with some singular support condition, that we will continue to call $\operatorname{Nilp}$ ) on the stack

$$ \operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}}(X\setminus x_{0})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{B}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}). $$

#### 0.1.10.

Using Faergeman’s construction of a tamely ramified spectral action in [Fae24] and our proof of the compact generation of $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G}^{\operatorname{I}})$ in [Nam24], we are able to emulate [GR24a] to construct a functor

$$ \mathbb{L}_{G}^{\operatorname{I}}:\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{G}^{\operatorname{I}})\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{LocSys}_{\check{G}}(X\setminus x_{0})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{B}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}})). $$

#### 0.1.11.

Following the strategy of the five papers, the next logical step is to study $\mathbb{L}_{G}^{\operatorname{I}}$ locally. Since away from $x_{0}$ the functor is unramified, we should more specifically study it locally at $x_{0}$ . The three pointwise equivalences in the unramified setting have natural Iwahori-ramified counterparts: these are the Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov equivalence

$$ \operatorname{AB}_{x_{0}}:\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}, $$

Bezrukavnikov’s equivalence

$$ \operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}:\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}, $$

and the Iwahori Fundamental Local Equivalence

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}:\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{B}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}). $$

#### 0.1.12.

We expect these pointwise equivalences to interact with $\mathbb{L}_{G}^{\operatorname{I}}$ in an entirely analogous way to the unramified setting, but we again do not expect this to be sufficient. We want to allow $x\in X$ to vary in families, but because the Iwahori subgroup is not factorizable, we do not want to allow $x_{0}$ to move around. In fact, we want to allow families of tuples of points in $X$ that contain the constant family with value $x_{0}$ so we can consider what happens when the ”mobile” point $x$ ”collides” with the ”stationary” point $x_{0}$ .

#### 0.1.13.

The technical device we propose to use in this case is the theory of Factorization Module Categories. To be a bit more precise, we will consider pairs $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{M})$ consisting of $\mathcal{C}$ , a factorization category and $\mathcal{M}$ , a factorization $\mathcal{C}$ -module category at $x_{0}$ .

#### 0.1.14.

In this paper, we will show that each of the six local Iwahori-ramified categories at $x_{0}$ can be endowed with the structure of factorization module category over the factorization category corresponding to its unramified analogue. Furthermore, we will upgrade the three pointwise Iwahori-ramified equivalences to equivalences of pairs

$$ \operatorname{AB}:(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}))\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})), $$

$$ \operatorname{B}:(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}(\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}), $$

and

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}:(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}(\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})). $$

### 0.2. Main Results

#### 0.2.1.

Here are the main results in this paper.

#### 0.2.2.

In Section 1, we construct the six factorization module categories that are of interest to us. We will think of them and denote them as pairs $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{M})$ consisting of a factorization category $\mathcal{C}$ and a factorization $\mathcal{C}$ -module category (at $x_{0}$ ) $\mathcal{M}$ . In all six cases, the factorization categories (i.e. the first components) are defined in [ABC+24a].

#### Proposition 0.2.3.

[ABC+24a] There is an equivalence, called the geometric Casselman-Shalika equivalence, of factorization categories

$$ \operatorname{CS}_{G}:\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}) $$

in $\operatorname{FactAlgCat}$ .

#### 0.2.4.

In Section 2, we construct a morphism of pairs

$$ \operatorname{AB}:(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}))\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

whose first component is $\operatorname{CS}_{G}$ . We also prove

#### Theorem 0.2.5.

The morphism of pairs $\operatorname{AB}$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ .

#### Proposition 0.2.6.

[ABC+24a] There is a monoidal equivalence, called (derived) geometric Satake

$$ \operatorname{Sat}_{G}:\operatorname{Sph}_{G}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}} $$

in $\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{FactAlgCat})$ . The equivalence $\operatorname{CS}_{G}$ is equivariant with respect to $\operatorname{Sat}_{G}$ .

#### 0.2.7.

In Section 3, we construct a morphism of monoidal pairs

$$ \operatorname{B}:(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}) $$

whose first component is $\operatorname{Sat}_{G}$ . We also prove

#### Theorem 0.2.8.

The morphism of monoidal pairs $\operatorname{B}$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}})$ , such that the equivalence of pairs $\operatorname{AB}$ is equivariant with respect to it.

#### Proposition 0.2.9.

[ABC+24a] There is an equivalence, called the Fundamental Local Equivalence, of factorization categories

$$ \operatorname{FLE}:\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}) $$

that is equivariant with respect to $\operatorname{Sat}_{G}$ .

#### 0.2.10.

In Section 4, we construct a morphism of pairs

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}:(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})\longrightarrow(\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

whose first component is $\operatorname{FLE}$ . We also prove

#### Theorem 0.2.11.

The morphism of pairs $\operatorname{IFLE}$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ that is equivariant with respect to $\operatorname{B}$ .

### 0.3. The Structure of the Paper

#### 0.3.1.

We will now outline the structure of this paper.

#### 0.3.2.

We begin by recalling the basics of factorization in Subsection 1.1. We do this mainly to fix notation, and refer the reader to [Ras] for details.

#### 0.3.3.

In Subsections 1.2, 1.3, and 1.4, we define the six factorization module categories that appear on either side of $\operatorname{AB}$ , $\operatorname{B}$ , and $\operatorname{IFLE}$ respectively.

#### 0.3.4.

In Subsection 1.5, we prove Theorem 1.5.6, which allows us to approximate various factorization module categories by categories of factorization modules. This will be used to construct $\operatorname{B}$ and $\operatorname{IFLE}$ . This is a factorization module categorical version of Proposition 1.5.4, which, informally speaking, approximates factorization categories by categories of factorization modules, and was proven in [ABC+24a].

#### 0.3.5.

The next three sections are each devoted to constructing the equivalences $\operatorname{AB}$ , $\operatorname{B}$ , and $\operatorname{IFLE}$ respectively.

#### 0.3.6.

In Subsection 2.1, we discuss the notion of Fusability, which will appear in an upcoming paper [BCG26] of Bogdanova, Chen, and Gaitsgory. Fusability is a condition on factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ -module categories that can be checked combinatorially, and it allows us to reduce showing that a functor between factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ -module categories is an equivalence to showing that the fiber at $x_{0}$ is an equivalence of plain categories. We argue that $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ is fusable.

#### 0.3.7.

In Subsection 2.2, we construct the morphism of pairs $\operatorname{AB}$ using a semi-infinite version constructed in [CCF+24]. Loc. cit. also shows that semi-infinite version of $\operatorname{AB}$ is a pointwise equivalence, which allows us to conclude that $\operatorname{AB}_{x_{0}}$ is an equivalence in Subsection 2.3, thereby proving Theorem 0.2.5.

#### 0.3.8.

In Subsection 3.1, we show that the 2-functor of factorization restriction, defined in the unpublished document [CF] of Chen and Fu, along $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ is conservative. Because the image of $\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ under this functor is fusable, this will allow us to reduce showing that $\operatorname{B}$ is an equivalence to showing that $\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}$ is an equivalence.

#### 0.3.9.

In Subsection 3.2, we construct the monoidal morphism of pairs $\operatorname{B}$ using the action of $\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ on $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})$ via $\operatorname{AB}$ . To show that $\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}$ is an equivalence, in Subsection 3.3 we adapt ideas of Dhillon and Taylor contained in [DT25] from the Betti setting. This proves Theorem 0.2.8.

#### 0.3.10.

In Subsection 4.1, we construct $\operatorname{IFLE}$ . In Subsection 4.2, we argue that $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ is compactly generated and that $\operatorname{IFLE}$ preserves compacts, in order to reduce showing that $\operatorname{IFLE}$ is an equivalence to showing that $\operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}$ is an equivalence.

#### 0.3.11.

In Subsection 4.3, we introduce the notion of Iwahori-Hecke Temperedness. This is a condition on $\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}$ -module categories that implies that tensoring $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}-$ is conservative.

#### 0.3.12.

Finally, in Subsection 4.4, we use the compatibility between $\operatorname{B}$ and $\operatorname{IFLE}$ to embed $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}-$ applied to both sides of $\operatorname{IFLE}$ in an ambient category $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})$ . Then we show that these embeddings match, and that the two sides of $\operatorname{IFLE}$ are Iwahori-Hecke tempered to conclude the proof of Theorem 0.2.11.

## 1. Factorization

### 1.1. Factorization Basics

In this subsection, we will briefly review some definitions and concepts related to factorization. The purpose of this is mainly to fix notation; for a detailed discussion, see [Ras].

#### 1.1.1.

Throughout this paper, we will fix for all time a smooth, projective, connected curve $X$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero. We will also fix a closed point $x_{0}\in X$ .

#### 1.1.2.

We begin by fixing notation for the spaces on which our factorization objects will live. Informally speaking, the pattern is as follows: our ”algebra-like” objects (factorization categories, factorization algebras, factorization spaces) will live on $\operatorname{Ran}$ , and after fixing an ”algebra-object”, a ”module-like” object of the corresponding type (factorization module categories, factorization modules, factorization module spaces) will live on $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ . This is because for us, the intended application of factorization ”module-like” objects are to study level structure at the fixed point $x_{0}$ .

#### Definition 1.1.3.

Denote by $\operatorname{Ran}$ the unital Ran (categorical) prestack of $X$ . For a test affine scheme $S$ ,

$$ \operatorname{Ran}(S)=\{finite\ subsets\ of\ X_{dR}(S)\} $$

which is considered as a partially ordered set under inclusion.

#### Remark 1.1.4.

We are taking the convention that $\operatorname{Ran}$ without any decorations is the unital version of Ran space, while other sources may use the same notation to mean the non-unital version, whose outputs are the set of finite subsets of $X_{dR}(S)$ rather than the poset (and possibly excluding the empty subset). From now on, everything related to factorization will refer to the unital version by default unless explicitly stated otherwise. One exception is that factorization functors (i.e. morphisms of factorization categories and factorization module categories) are allowed to be $\emph{lax}$ -unital rather than strictly unital.

#### 1.1.5.

A variant of this is the prestack $\operatorname{Ran}^{\subset}$ , which classifies ordered pairs of finite subsets of $X$ such that the first is contained in the second. There are projection maps

$$ \operatorname{pr}_{\operatorname{small}},\operatorname{pr}_{\operatorname{big}}:\operatorname{Ran}^{\subset}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ran} $$

sending a pair $A\subset B\subset X_{dR}(S)$ to $A$ and $B$ respectively.

#### Definition 1.1.6.

Let $Y\to\operatorname{Ran}$ be a morphism. Then denote

$$ \operatorname{Ran}_{Y}=Y\underset{\operatorname{Ran}}{\times}\operatorname{Ran}^{\subset} $$

where $\operatorname{pr}_{\operatorname{small}}$ is used to form the fiber product. Then there is a map

$$ \operatorname{pr}_{\operatorname{big},Y}:\operatorname{Ran}_{Y}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ran} $$

induced by $\operatorname{pr}_{\operatorname{big}}:\operatorname{Ran}^{\subset}\to\operatorname{Ran}$ . The most important case for us is when $Y=\operatorname{pt}$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Ran}$ is given by the singleton containing $x_{0}$ . In this case, we denote the corresponding prestack by $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ .

#### Remark 1.1.7.

For a test affine scheme $S$ , $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}(S)$ classifies finite subsets of $X_{dR}(S)$ containing the constant map $S\to\operatorname{pt}\overset{x_{0}}{\to}X_{dR}$ . Thus, $\operatorname{pr}_{\operatorname{big},x_{0}}:\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}\to\operatorname{Ran}$ is an inclusion.

#### 1.1.8.

Next, we will define the notion of factorization category. Intuitively, this is a way to assign a category to each tuple of points $\underline{x}\subset X$ in families, in a way that cares about the collisions of points. Consider the subset

$$ [\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}]_{disj}\subset\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran} $$

classifying disjoint pairs of finite subsets of $X$ . Then form the diagram

$$ \operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}\supset[\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}]_{disj}\overset{\cup}{\to}\operatorname{Ran}. $$

#### Definition 1.1.9.

A factorization category is a sheaf of categories $\mathcal{C}$ on $\operatorname{Ran}$ together with factorization data, which consists of an equivalence

$$ (\mathcal{C}\boxtimes\mathcal{C})|_{disj}\simeq\cup^{*}\mathcal{C} $$

as well as higher homotopy coherences. We will denote the category of factorization categories by $\operatorname{FactAlgCat}$ .

#### 1.1.10.

To define the notion of factorization module category (at $x_{0}$ ), we will consider the subset

$$ [\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}]_{disj}\subset\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}} $$

defined in the obvious way. We can again form a diagram

$$ \operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}\supset[\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}]_{disj}\overset{\cup}{\to}\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}. $$

#### Definition 1.1.11.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a factorization category. A factorization $\mathcal{C}$ -module category (at $x_{0}$ ) is a sheaf of categories $\mathcal{M}$ on $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ together with factorization module data over $\mathcal{C}$ , which consists of an equivalence

$$ (\mathcal{C}\boxtimes\mathcal{M})|_{disj}\simeq\cup^{*}\mathcal{M} $$

as well as higher homotopy coherences. We will denote the category of factorization $\mathcal{C}$ -module categories by $\mathcal{C}-\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ .

#### Remark 1.1.12.

Instead of fixing a factorization category $\mathcal{C}$ , we sometimes wish to consider pairs $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{M})$ , where $\mathcal{M}$ is a factorization $\mathcal{C}$ -module category. The category of such pairs is denoted $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ , and a morphism

$$ (\mathcal{C}_{1},\mathcal{M}_{1})\to(\mathcal{C}_{2},\mathcal{M}_{2}) $$

in this category consists of a factorization functor (i.e. a morphism in $\operatorname{FactAlgCat}$ )

$$ \mathcal{C}_{1}\to\mathcal{C}_{2} $$

and a morphism of sheaf of categories (on $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ )

$$ \mathcal{M}_{1}\to\mathcal{M}_{2} $$

compatible with the above factorization functor.

#### 1.1.13.

We will now discuss factorization structures on the level of objects.

#### Definition 1.1.14.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a factorization category. A factorization algebra $a$ in $\mathcal{C}$ is a global section of $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with factorization data, which consists of an isomorphism

$$ (a\boxtimes a)|_{disj}\simeq\cup^{!}a $$

as well as higher homotopy coherences. We denote the category of factorization algebras in $\mathcal{C}$ by $\operatorname{FactAlg(\mathcal{C})}$ .

#### Definition 1.1.15.

Let $Y\to\operatorname{Ran}$ . Furthermore, let $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{M})\in\operatorname{FactModCat}_{Y}$ (whose definition is obtained by replacing $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ by $\operatorname{Ran}_{Y}$ in the definition of $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ ) be a pair. Then for a factorization algebra $a$ in $\mathcal{C}$ and any $Z\to\operatorname{Ran}_{Y}$ , a factorization $a$ -module $m$ in $\mathcal{M}$ at $Z$ is a section of $\mathcal{M}$ on $Z$ equipped with factorization module data over $a$ , which consists of an isomorphism

$$ (a\boxtimes m)|_{disj}\simeq\cup^{!}m $$

as well as higher homotopy coherences. Denote the category of such objects by $a\operatorname{-FactMod}_{Z}(\mathcal{M})$ .

#### 1.1.16.

The reason we define factorization modules for more than just $x_{0}$ is that we want to construct factorization categories and factorization module categories of factorization modules by letting $Z$ vary.

#### Definition 1.1.17.

Let $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{M})\in\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ and let $a\in\operatorname{FactAlg}(\mathcal{C})$ . Consider the sheaf of categories

$$ a\operatorname{-FactMod}(\mathcal{C}) $$

on $\operatorname{Ran}$ that assigns to each test affine scheme $S$ over $\operatorname{Ran}$ the category $a\operatorname{-FactMod}_{S}(\mathcal{C})$ . This has the natural structure of a factorization category. Furthermore, consider the sheaf of categories

$$ a\operatorname{-FactMod}(\mathcal{M}) $$

on $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ that assigns to each test affine scheme $S$ over $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ the category $a\operatorname{-FactMod}_{S}(\mathcal{M})$ . This has the natural structure of a factorization $a\operatorname{-FactMod}(\mathcal{C})$ -module category at $x_{0}$ .

#### 1.1.18.

We have described an algebraic method for producing factorization categories and factorization module categories. We will finish this subsection by describing a geometric way to produce factorization categories and factorization module categories.

#### Definition 1.1.19.

A factorization space is a space $\mathcal{Y}\to\operatorname{Ran}$ equipped with factorization data, which includes an isomorphism

$$ (\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Y})\underset{\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}}{\times}[\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}]_{disj}\simeq\mathcal{Y}\underset{\operatorname{Ran},\cup}{\times}[\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}]_{disj}. $$

#### Definition 1.1.20.

A factorization $\mathcal{Y}$ -module space (at $x_{0}$ ) is a space $\mathcal{Z}\to\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ equipped with factorization module data over $\mathcal{Y}$ , which includes an isomorphism

$$ (\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\underset{\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}{\times}[\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}]_{disj}\simeq\mathcal{Z}\underset{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}},\cup}{\times}[\operatorname{Ran}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}]_{disj}. $$

#### 1.1.21.

Given a ”nice” sheaf theory with pullbacks and Kunneth formula, for example $\operatorname{QCoh}$ , a factorization space $\mathcal{Y}$ gives rise to a factorization category via

$$ (S\to\operatorname{Ran})\mapsto\operatorname{QCoh}(S\times_{\operatorname{Ran}}\mathcal{Y}) $$

and a factorization $\mathcal{Y}$ -module space $\mathcal{Z}$ gives rise to a factorization $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal{Y})$ -module category via

$$ (S\to\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}})\mapsto\operatorname{QCoh}(S\times_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}\mathcal{Z}). $$

### 1.2. Main Characters of AB

In this subsection and the two that follow, we will recall or define the various objects of $\operatorname{FactAlgCat}$ and $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ that will appear throughout this paper.

#### 1.2.1.

We begin by recalling the definition of the factorization category $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)$ given in Section 1.3 of [ABC+24a]. In order to do so, we first consider the Ran Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}}$ . For a test affine scheme $S$ and $\underline{x}:S\to\operatorname{Ran}$ , a lift of $\underline{x}$ to $\operatorname{Gr}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}}$ is given by a pair

$$ (\mathcal{P}_{G},\alpha) $$

of a principal $G$ -bundle $\mathcal{P}_{G}$ on $S\times X$ , and a trivialization

$$ \alpha:\mathcal{P}_{G}|_{(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{\underline{x}}}\simeq\mathcal{P}_{G}^{triv} $$

of $\mathcal{P}_{G}$ on the complement of the graph of $\underline{x}$ in $S\times X$ .

#### 1.2.2.

The Ran Grassmannian naturally has the structure of a (unital) factorization space, so we can produce a (unital) factorization category $\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})$ (for a discussion of critically twisted D-modules, see Section 1.1 of [ABC+24a]) defined by

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})_{S}=\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(S\times_{\operatorname{Ran}}\operatorname{Gr}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}}). $$

Furthermore, there is an action of the factorization group ind-scheme $LG_{\operatorname{Ran}}$ (and thus of the factorization subgroup ind-scheme $LN_{\operatorname{Ran}}$ ) on $\operatorname{Gr}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}}$ , and basically what we would like to do now is define $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)$ as the Whittaker invariant category of $\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})$ , i.e. as

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})^{(LN,\chi)} $$

or more precisely,

$$ S\mapsto\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Gr}_{G})_{S}^{(LN_{S},\chi_{S})}. $$

#### 1.2.3.

However, we must incorporate the geometric twisting construction from Section 1.2 of [ABC+24a], which we briefly repeat now.

Let $H\subset G$ is a subgroup, and let $Y$ be a space living over $X$ equipped with an $L^{+}H$ -action. Also, let $\mathcal{P}_{H}$ be a principal $H$ -bundle on $X$ . Then the twist of $Y$ by $\mathcal{P}_{H}$ is

$$ Y_{\mathcal{P}_{H}}=Y\times^{L^{+}H}(\mathcal{P}_{H}|_{D^{\times}})=(Y\times(\mathcal{P}_{H}|_{D^{\times}}))/L^{+}H. $$

In our case, we apply (a factorizable version of) the above construction to $\operatorname{Gr_{G,\operatorname{Ran}}}$ , taking $H=T$ and $\mathcal{P}_{T}$ to be the factorization $T$ -principal bundle $\rho(\omega_{X})=2\rho(\omega_{X}^{\otimes\frac{1}{2}})$ .

Since $LN$ is normalized by $L^{+}T$ , we can take the twist $LN_{\rho(\omega_{X})}$ . This is a (factorization) group ind-scheme which acts on $\operatorname{Gr_{G,\operatorname{Ran},\rho(\omega_{X})}}$ . Finally, we define

#### Definition 1.2.4.

The (unital) factorization category $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)\in\operatorname{FactAlgCat}$ is

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Gr}_{G,\rho(\omega_{X})})^{(LN_{\rho(\omega_{X})},\chi_{\rho(\omega_{X})})}. $$

#### 1.2.5.

Next, we will define the factorization $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)$ -module category (at the point $x_{0}$ ) $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ . Let $\operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}$ be the following. For a test affine scheme $S$ and $\underline{x}:S\to\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ , a lift of $\underline{x}$ to $\operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}$ is given by a quadruple

$$ (\mathcal{P}_{G},\alpha,\mathcal{P}_{B},\gamma) $$

of a principal $G$ -bundle $\mathcal{P}_{G}$ on $S\times X$ , a trivialization

$$ \alpha:\mathcal{P}_{G}|_{(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{\underline{x}}}\simeq\mathcal{P}_{G}^{triv} $$

of $\mathcal{P}_{G}$ on the complement of the graph of $\underline{x}$ in $S\times X$ , and a reduction of structure group to $B$

$$ \gamma:\mathcal{P}_{B}\times^{B}G\simeq\mathcal{P}_{G}|_{S\times\{x_{0}\}} $$

on $S\times\{x_{0}\}$ .

#### 1.2.6.

$\operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}$ naturally has the structure of a factorization module space over the Ran Grassmannian. Furthermore, there is an action of the factorization module group ind-scheme $LG_{\operatorname{Ran_{x_{0}}}}$ (i.e. the restriction of $LG_{\operatorname{Ran}}$ to $\operatorname{Ran_{x_{0}}}\subset\operatorname{Ran}$ considered as a group object in factorization module spaces over $LG_{\operatorname{Ran}}$ ) on $\operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}$ . Thus we can define $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ in the same way as $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)$ mutatis mutandis, by forming the twist

$$ \operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}},\rho(\omega_{X})} $$

and taking twisted Whittaker invariants

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}},\rho(\omega_{X})})^{(LN_{\rho(\omega_{X})},\chi_{\rho(\omega_{X})})}. $$

#### Definition 1.2.7.

The pair $(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}))\in\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ consists of the factorization category $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)$ and the factorization $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G)$ -module category

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})=\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G,\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}},\rho(\omega_{X})})^{(LN_{\rho(\omega_{X})},\chi_{\rho(\omega_{X})})}. $$

#### 1.2.8.

Now we move on to the spectral side. In order to define the factorization category $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ and the factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ -module category $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})$ , we will recall the definition of regular and meromorphic local systems. A more thorough version of the discussion that will take up the remainder of this subsection can be found in Appendices B.3-B.7 of [ABC+24a].

#### 1.2.9.

For an algebraic group $H$ , the factorization space of regular $H$ -local systems on the formal disk $\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{reg}}$ is defined as follows.

Given a test affine scheme $S$ and an $S$ -point $\underline{x}:S\to\operatorname{Ran}$ , the formal disk around $\underline{x}$ is defined as the $X$ -scheme

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x}}=(S\times X)\underset{S_{dR}\times X_{dR}}{\times}\Gamma_{\underline{x},dR} $$

this descends to an $X_{dR}$ -scheme since we can define

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x},\nabla}=(S\times X_{dR})\underset{S_{dR}\times X_{dR}}{\times}\Gamma_{\underline{x},dR}=S\underset{S_{dR}}{\times}\Gamma_{\underline{x},dR}. $$

and

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x}}=\hat{D}_{\underline{x},\nabla}\times_{X_{dR}}X. $$

#### 1.2.10.

Let $Y_{\nabla}$ be a space over $X_{dR}$ , and denote

$$ Y=Y_{\nabla}\times_{X_{dR}}X. $$

Now we will define the factorization space called the horizontal arc space of $Y$ that is denoted by $L_{\nabla}^{+}Y$ . A lift of $\underline{x}$ to $L_{\nabla}^{+}Y$ is given by an $X_{dR}$ -map

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x},\nabla}\to Y_{\nabla}. $$

#### 1.2.11.

We now define

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{reg}}=L_{\nabla}^{+}(\operatorname{pt}/H\times X). $$

In other words, a lift of $\underline{x}$ to $\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{reg}}$ is given by the data of an $X_{dR}$ -map

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x},\nabla}\to\operatorname{pt}/H\times X_{dR}. $$

or equivalently a map

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x},\nabla}\to\operatorname{pt}/H. $$

#### Definition 1.2.12.

The factorization category $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})\in\operatorname{FactAlgCat}$ is defined as

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}). $$

#### 1.2.13.

The factorization space of meromorphic $H$ -local systems on the formal disk $\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{mer}}$ is more subtle to define. For a test affine scheme $S$ and an $S$ -point $\underline{x}:S\to\operatorname{Ran}$ , we note that $\hat{D}_{\underline{x}}$ is an ind-affine ind-scheme. Writing

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x}}=\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Spec}(A_{i}), $$

we denote

$$ D_{\underline{x}}=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{lim}A_{i}), $$

or, in other words, we take the colimit in the category of affine schemes instead. The punctured formal disk around $\underline{x}$ is then defined to be

$$ D_{\underline{x}}^{\times}=D_{\underline{x}}\setminus\Gamma_{\underline{x}}. $$

#### Example 1.2.14.

If we take $S=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ and $\underline{x}$ to be the singleton set containing only $x\in X$ , and we let $t$ be a local coordinate of $X$ at $x$ , then

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x}}=\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]/t^{i})=\operatorname{Spf}(k[[t]]) $$

and

$$ D_{\underline{x}}=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{lim}k[t]/t^{i})=\operatorname{Spec}(k[[t]]). $$

In this case,

$$ D_{\underline{x}}^{\times}=\operatorname{Spec}(k((t))). $$

#### 1.2.15.

According to Appendix A.1 in [Bog24], the $X$ -schemes $D_{\underline{x}}$ and $D_{\underline{x}}^{\times}$ both descend over $X_{dR}$ . We denote the descents by

$$ D_{\underline{x},\nabla} $$

and

$$ D_{\underline{x},\nabla}^{\times} $$

respectively. If $Y_{\nabla}\to X_{dR}$ is affine, an $X_{dR}$ -map

$$ \hat{D}_{\underline{x},\nabla}\to Y_{\nabla} $$

is equivalent to an $X_{dR}$ -map

$$ D_{\underline{x},\nabla}\to Y_{\nabla} $$

so we can define the horizontal loop space of $Y$ , $L_{\nabla}Y$ as the factorization space such that a lift of $\underline{x}$ to $L_{\nabla}Y$ is given by an $X_{dR}$ -map

$$ D_{\underline{x},\nabla}^{\times}\to Y_{\nabla}. $$

#### Remark 1.2.16.

We emphasize that we are only defining $L_{\nabla}Y$ for affine $Y_{\nabla}\to X_{dR}$ . This is because we want there to be a map

$$ L_{\nabla}^{+}Y\to L_{\nabla}Y $$

induced by

$$ D_{\underline{x},\nabla}^{\times}\to D_{\underline{x},\nabla}. $$

Because of this, we cannot simply define $\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{mer}}=L_{\nabla}(\operatorname{pt}/H\times X)$ , since $\operatorname{pt}/H\times X_{dR}$ is not affine over $X_{dR}$ .

#### 1.2.17.

Next we will introduce the Jets construction, which is described in Appendix B.5 of [ABC+24a]. For a prestack $Y\to X$ , we can produce an $X_{dR}$ -prestack

$$ \operatorname{Jets}(Y)\to X_{dR} $$

whose $S$ -points are pairs consisting of $x:S\to X_{dR}$ and an $X$ -map

$$ \hat{D}_{x}\to Y. $$

This gives us a way to express $L^{+}Y$ , the factorization arc space of $Y$ , as

$$ L^{+}Y=L_{\nabla}^{+}\operatorname{Jets}(Y) $$

Furthermore, if $Y\to X$ is affine, then $\operatorname{Jets}(Y)\to X_{dR}$ is also affine, and we can express $LY$ , the factorization loop space of $Y$ , as

$$ LY=L_{\nabla}\operatorname{Jets}(Y). $$

#### 1.2.18.

Now we are ready to define $\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{mer}}$ . To motivate the definition, we note that as group objects over $X_{dR}$ ,

$$ H\times X_{dR}\subset\operatorname{Jets}(H\times X) $$

and the quotient

$$ \operatorname{Jets}(H\times X)/(H\times X_{dR})=\operatorname{Jets}(\mathfrak{h}\otimes\omega_{X}) $$

the latter which we will denote by $\operatorname{Conn}(\mathfrak{h})$ . Note that this is affine over $X_{dR}$ since $\mathfrak{h}\otimes\omega_{X}$ is affine (in fact, a vector bundle) over $X$ . Then

$$ \operatorname{pt}/H\times X_{dR}=(\operatorname{pt}\times X_{dR})/(H\times X_{dR})=\operatorname{Conn}(\mathfrak{h})/\operatorname{Jets}(H\times X) $$

and thus

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{reg}}=L_{\nabla}^{+}(\operatorname{pt}/H\times X)=L_{\nabla}^{+}\operatorname{Jets}(\mathfrak{h}\otimes\omega_{X})/L_{\nabla}^{+}\operatorname{Jets}(H\times X)=L_{\nabla}^{+}\operatorname{Conn}(\mathfrak{h})/L^{+}H. $$

Defining

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{mer}}=L_{\nabla}\operatorname{Conn}(\mathfrak{h})/LH $$

gives a map

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{reg}}\to\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{mer}} $$

as desired.

#### 1.2.19.

We will finish this subsection by giving the definition of the factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ -module category $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})$ . We could of course form the factorization space

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{\check{B}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}^{\operatorname{reg}}, $$

but we want a version of this as a factorization module space over $\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}$ at $x_{0}$ . Denote by $\operatorname{LS}_{H}(D_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}^{\times})$ the factorization space (defined in Definition 3.1.8 of [Bog24]) such that the lifts of $\underline{x}:S\to\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ to $\operatorname{LS}_{H}(D_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}^{\times})$ are given by

$$ \{D_{\underline{x},\nabla}\underset{X_{dR}}{\times}(X\setminus x_{0})_{dR}\to\operatorname{Conn}(\mathfrak{h})\}/\{D_{\underline{x},\nabla}\underset{X_{dR}}{\times}(X\setminus x_{0})_{dR}\to H\}. $$

Since $D_{S\times x_{0},\nabla}\subset D_{\underline{x},\nabla}$ , there is a map via restriction

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{H}(D_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}^{\times})\to\operatorname{LS}_{H}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times}) $$

where the latter is the fiber of $\operatorname{LS}_{H}^{\operatorname{mer}}$ at $\{x_{0}\}\in\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ .

We define ${\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}$ to be the factorization $\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}$ -module space

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}^{\times})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{B}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D_{x_{0}}). $$

#### Definition 1.2.20.

The pair $(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\in\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ consists of the factorization category $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ and the factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ -module category

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})=\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}). $$

#### Remark 1.2.21.

The fiber of $\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}$ at $\{x_{0}\}\in\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ is

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{\check{B}}(D^{\times})\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D^{\times})}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{T}}(D) $$

which identifies with the smooth, finite dimensional stack

$$ \tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}=\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B} $$

and the fiber of the sheaf of categories $\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}})$ is thus the usual category

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}) $$

which is why we abusively denote the factorization module category using the same name.

#### 3.3.2.

In [DT25], Dhillon and Taylor construct a version of (pointwise) Bezrukavnikov’s equivalence in the monodromic, Betti setting. In other words, there are two key differences from our setting. First, the stack on the geometric side is

$$ \tilde{\operatorname{Fl}}_{G}/I_{0}=I_{0}\backslash LG/I_{0} $$

instead of

$$ \operatorname{Fl}_{G}/I=I\backslash LG/I. $$

Second, the sheaf theory on the geometric side is ind-constructible sheaves with nilpotent singular support

$$ \operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Nilp}} $$

instead of

$$ \operatorname{D-mod} $$

and correspondingly, the spaces that appear on the spectral side are the Betti versions.

#### 3.3.3.

Let us summarize the construction in [DT25] (or, rather, the analogue of their construction in our unipotent monodromy, de Rham setting). The monoidal category

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})} $$

has an obvious action on the category

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}) $$

which can be identified via $\operatorname{AB}_{x_{0}}$ with

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

$$ \operatorname{bi-Whit}(LG)=\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(LG)) $$

on $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ . However, the latter action can be identified with the action of

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}) $$

on $\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G})$ via pullback. Thus, we obtain a monoidal functor

$$ \iota^{!}:\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G})}(\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}))\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

#### 3.3.4.

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}/\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren}),\leq-\infty}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

#### 3.3.7.

Therefore, all that remains to be shown is that the datum of compatibility - between the action of $\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}$ on $\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G})$ and the action of $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G})$ - given by $\Psi_{x_{0}}\circ\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}$ is isomorphic to the tautological one. $$ (\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

generates the target; therefore, to show that the essential image of

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}, $$

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\overset{\operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

is essentially surjective.

Since the functor is fully faithful, it suffices to show that it generates the target; for which, in turn, it suffices to show that the composition

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

generates the target.

Because we have

$$ (\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}})_{\operatorname{red}}=\bigsqcup_{\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\in\check{\lambda}^{+}}\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}, $$

the objects

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}\in\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

compactly generate $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}$ .

We claim that the Verma modules

$$ \mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}=\operatorname{ind}_{I}^{(\hat{g}_{\operatorname{crit}},I)}k_{\check{\lambda}}\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} $$

are sent to $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}$ under the functor $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}$ .

To see this, we will adapt the argument in [FG10] that shows $\operatorname{FLE}$ sends the Weyl modules $\mathbb{V}^{\check{\lambda}}$ to $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{reg}}}$ :

On one hand, we have the isomorphism

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}\simeq\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}) $$

and unwinding definitions yields

$$ \operatorname{End}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})=\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{ind}_{I}^{(\hat{g}_{\operatorname{crit}},I)}k_{\check{\lambda}},\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{I}(k_{\check{\lambda}},\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})=:(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})_{\check{\check{\lambda}}}^{I^{0}}. $$

For any $M\in\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}$ , there is a map

$$ (M)_{\check{\lambda}}^{I^{0}}\to M^{\hat{\mathfrak{n}}_{+}}\to H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],M\otimes\Psi_{0}), $$

which is the content of Lemma 3 of [FG10]. Taking $M=\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ gives us a map

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}\to H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\otimes\Psi_{0}), $$

where the latter identifies with the desired image of $\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ . Thus, it suffices to show that this map is an isomorphism.

Analogously to the $\check{\lambda}$ -regular case, we have that the above map has the structure of a morphism of modules over the lie algebroid $N^{*}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}/\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}$ , and that $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}$ is irreducible as a $N^{*}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}/\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}$ -module. Therefore, this map must be injective and it suffices to compute and compare the characters of both sides as in Section 5 of [FG10].

First, let us compute the character of $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}$ . Let

$$ J=\{\alpha_{i}\in\Delta|\langle\alpha_{i},\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\rangle=0\} $$

and denote by $\check{P}_{J}$ the parabolic subgroup of $\check{G}$ corresponding to $J$ . Now note that $\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}$ is the set of operators of the form

$$ \{\partial_{t}+\Sigma_{\Delta}\ t^{\langle\alpha_{i},\check{\lambda}\rangle}f_{i}+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]],w\in O\} $$

modulo the action of $\check{N}[[t]]$ , where

$$ O=\{w\in\check{\mathfrak{b}}\ |\ w+\Sigma_{J}f_{i}\operatorname{mod}\check{\mathfrak{n}}_{J}\in\mathcal{N}_{\check{\mathfrak{m}}_{J}}\}. $$

However, this is the same as

$$ \{\partial_{t}+\frac{1}{t}(\Sigma_{\Delta}f_{i}-(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}))+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1},w\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)O(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\} $$

modulo the free action of $(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{N}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}$ .

Consider $O\cap\check{\mathfrak{m}}_{J}$ , which carries a free and transitive action of the group $\check{N}\cap\check{M}_{J}$ . There is a surjective homomorphism of groups

$$ \phi:(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{N}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\to\check{N}\cap\check{M}_{J} $$

which picks out the constant term, and there is a surjective morphism

$$ \displaystyle\{\partial_{t}+\frac{1}{t}(\Sigma_{\Delta}f_{i}-(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}))+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1},w\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)O(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\} \displaystyle\overset{\pi}{\longrightarrow}O\cap\check{\mathfrak{m}}_{J} $$

which picks out the constant term of $w$ . $\pi$ is equivariant with respect to $\phi$ , so we have

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}\simeq\pi^{-1}(0)/\operatorname{ker}(\phi) $$

and thus

$$ \operatorname{char}(\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}})=\operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\pi^{-1}(0)))/\operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{ker}(\phi))). $$

$\pi^{-1}(0)$ is

$$ \{\partial_{t}+\frac{1}{t}(\Sigma_{\Delta}f_{i}-(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}))+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1},w\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{n}}_{J}(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\} $$

so

$$ \operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\pi^{-1}(0)))=\Pi_{n>0}(1-q)^{-l}\cdot(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+1})^{-1})\cdot(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi^{+}\setminus\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+\langle\alpha,\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\rangle})^{-1}). $$

On the other hand,

$$ \operatorname{ker}(\phi)=(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{N}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\cap\operatorname{exp}(t\check{\mathfrak{n}}[[t]]) $$

so

$$ \operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{ker}(\phi)))=(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+1})^{-1})\cdot(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi^{+}\setminus\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+\langle\alpha,\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\rangle})^{-1}). $$

Therefore,

$$ \operatorname{char}(\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}})=\Pi_{n>0}(1-q)^{-l}. $$

Finally, to compute the character of $H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\otimes\Psi_{0})$ , we follow what is done in Section 5.2 of [FG10] essentially verbatim except with the finite Weyl module $V^{\lambda}$ replaced with the finite Verma module $M^{\lambda}$ . Then, we find that

$$ \operatorname{char}(H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\otimes\Psi_{0}))=\Pi_{n>0}(1-q)^{-l} $$

as desired. ∎

#### Proposition 4.4.4.

$\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})$ is Iwahori-Hecke tempered.

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{IndCoh}((\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}\underset{(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) \displaystyle\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}((\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge})\underset{\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge})}{\otimes}\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}} $$

#### Remark 4.4.5.

Here the argument diverges significantly from the proof of the analogous result, Proposition 7.2.6 of [ABC+24a] given in Section 7.4. #### Lemma 4.4.6.

If

$$ \mathcal{F}\in\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec},\leq-\infty} $$

and

$$ c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{c}\subset\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{b}, $$

#### Proof.

which sends

$$ \Gamma^{\check{\lambda}}(\mathcal{F})=\mathcal{F}\star\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}. $$

#### Proposition 4.4.7.

$\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ is Iwahori-Hecke tempered.

#### Proof.

We want to show that

$$ \operatorname{temp}:\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{temp}} $$

is an equivalence. Since it is a colocalization, it suffices to show that it is conservative. Note that the functor $\operatorname{IFLE}^{\operatorname{temp}}$

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{temp}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})^{\operatorname{temp}}\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) $$

is an equivalence. Thus, since $\operatorname{IFLE}$ preserves compacts, so does $\operatorname{temp}$ . It follows that it suffices to show that $\operatorname{temp}$ is conservative on compact objects. However, all compacts are bounded in $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ , and using the fact that

$$ \operatorname{cone}(\operatorname{temp}(\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\to\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\in\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec},\leq-\infty} $$

we can conclude that the cone of the counit map

$$ \operatorname{cone}((\operatorname{temp}(c)\to c)\simeq\operatorname{cone}(\operatorname{temp}(\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\to\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\star c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\leq-\infty}. $$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{temp}(c)=0$ , then $c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\leq-\infty}$ which implies $c=0$ since c is also bounded. This shows that $\operatorname{temp}$ is conservative on compact objects, as desired. ∎
